label: San Francisco to Los Angeles
blurb: 11 days in October: fog, cliffs and city lights by car.

brief.destination: California coast, San Francisco to Los Angeles
brief.text: I want the Golden Gate Bridge in fog and San Francisco at night, then the Big Sur cliffs and McWay Falls at sunset. I am driving the whole way and happy to start early for dawn. In Los Angeles I am after the skyline, the beach at blue hour and street life after dark.

answer.title: California coast by car in October
answer.summary: Four nights in San Francisco for the Golden Gate, the hills and the bay at night, then Highway 1 south to Carmel for three days on the Big Sur coast. The drive to Los Angeles takes US-101 inland, which is faster and less exposed to slide closures than the southern Big Sur stretch of Highway 1, and rejoins the coast in Malibu for sunset. Los Angeles closes the trip with beaches, Hollywood and downtown at night.

spots.name: Painted Ladies, Alamo Square
spots.when: Late afternoon, sun on the facades
spots.tip: Stand on the upper lawn of Alamo Square across Steiner Street and compress the row of houses against the downtown towers with the 100-400. Late sun from the west lights the fronts directly.

spots.name: Twin Peaks, Christmas Tree Point
spots.tip: Set up at the low wall of the Christmas Tree Point lot and frame Market Street running straight into downtown, with the Bay Bridge behind. Bring a jacket, the wind up here is strong and cold.

spots.name: Golden Gate Bridge from Battery Spencer
spots.tip: Walk the short path from the Conzelman Road pullouts to the concrete battery and frame the north tower close with the city behind. Low fog often sits under the deck at dawn in October, so give it time to move.

spots.name: Fort Point
spots.tip: Stand on the seawall west of the fort and shoot up into the steel arch of the bridge's south end. Use the ND10 for several seconds to smooth the waves breaking against the wall.

spots.name: Baker Beach
spots.tip: Walk to the north end of the beach and use the rocks at the waterline as foreground for the bridge and the Marin Headlands. Keep shooting into blue hour when the bridge lights come on.

spots.name: Dragon Gate and Grant Avenue
spots.tip: Start at the gate on Bush Street and walk north up Grant Avenue under the lanterns, shooting the shopfronts and deliveries. Detour a block west to Stockton Street for the produce markets.

spots.name: Hyde Street cable car at Lombard Street
spots.tip: Stand on the Hyde Street sidewalk just above Lombard and wait for a car to crest the hill with Alcatraz and the bay behind it. The afternoon sun comes from behind you and lights the cars.

spots.name: Bay Bridge from Pier 14
spots.tip: Walk to the end of the pier and use the line of lamp posts as a lead-in towards the western span of the Bay Bridge. Exposures of 20 to 30 seconds smooth the water.

spots.name: Ina Coolbrith Park
spots.tip: Climb the steps from Taylor Street to the upper terrace and frame Coit Tower and the Bay Bridge against the sunrise. The 100-400 isolates the bridge towers above the North Beach rooftops.

spots.name: Sutro Baths
spots.tip: Walk down to the ruined pool walls and use them as foreground lines towards the ocean and Point Lobos rocks. Long exposures with the ND10 turn the surf into mist at sunset.

spots.name: San Francisco skyline from Treasure Island
spots.tip: Park along Avenue of the Palms and shoot across the water to the full skyline with the Bay Bridge on the left. The 24-70 at 50 to 70mm fills the frame without the shoreline.

spots.name: Palace of Fine Arts
spots.tip: Stand on the east shore of the lagoon and catch the rotunda and colonnade reflected in still water. Dawn is quiet and the light comes from behind you.

spots.name: Pigeon Point Lighthouse
spots.tip: Walk the bluff north of the light station and frame the tower above the rocky cove. The 100-400 compresses the tower against the surf from the Highway 1 turnout.

spots.name: Carmel Beach
spots.tip: Walk down from the foot of Ocean Avenue and use the white sand and the cypress-lined bluff as foreground for the sunset. Shoot the waves at a quarter second for texture.

spots.name: Point Lobos, Sea Lion Point
spots.tip: Take the Sea Lion Point Trail to the viewing area above the rocks and shoot the coves and surge channels below. Use the CPL to cut glare on the water and show the colour in the coves.

spots.name: Soberanes Point, Garrapata State Park
spots.when: Late afternoon, side light on the headland
spots.tip: Park at the Highway 1 turnout and walk the short loop around the point, framing the rocks and surf with Whale Peak behind. Quieter than the famous stops and good for long exposures.

spots.name: Bixby Creek Bridge
spots.tip: Shoot from the turnout on the north side of the bridge, looking south along the arch and the coast. Arrive early, the turnout fills well before sunset.

spots.name: Point Sur Lighthouse
spots.when: Morning, as the marine layer lifts
spots.tip: Stop at the Highway 1 turnouts north of the rock and isolate the lighthouse on its volcanic peak with the 100-400. Low fog around the base makes the strongest frame.

spots.name: Pfeiffer Beach, Keyhole Arch
spots.when: Late afternoon, waves through the arch
spots.tip: Walk south along the beach to face Keyhole Arch and time long exposures for waves rushing through the opening. In October the sun sets north of the arch line, so shoot the rock and backlit surf rather than waiting for a sunburst.

spots.name: McWay Falls
spots.tip: Take the Overlook Trail from Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park to the railing and frame the waterfall dropping onto the beach of the cove. October flow is low, so a slow shutter makes the most of the water.

spots.name: The Lone Cypress, 17-Mile Drive
spots.tip: Shoot from the viewing platform on 17-Mile Drive and use the 100-400 to isolate the tree on its rock above the surf. The drive charges a per-car entry fee at the gates.

spots.name: El Matador State Beach
spots.tip: Take the steep path and stairs down from the bluff lot and frame the sea stacks and arch from the waterline. Check the tide table, at high tide the arch is cut off.

spots.name: Venice Canals
spots.tip: Walk the canal paths around Linnie Canal Park and shoot the arched footbridges and houses reflected in still water. Mornings are calm and empty.

spots.name: Venice Skate Park
spots.tip: Stand at the rail above the bowls and use the 100-400 for tight action against the beach and palms. Ask before photographing anyone up close.

spots.name: Santa Monica Pier
spots.tip: Walk onto the sand north of the pier and shoot the Ferris wheel and pier pilings as the lights come on. A 15 to 30 second exposure smooths the surf under the deck.

spots.name: Hollywood Sign from Lake Hollywood Park
spots.when: Morning, sign lit from the east
spots.tip: Stand on the lawn of Lake Hollywood Park and frame the sign on the ridge above the hillside houses. Street parking is limited on residential roads, so follow the posted signs.

spots.name: Griffith Observatory
spots.tip: Shoot from the west terrace for the observatory dome against the sunset, then move to the south side for the downtown towers and the grid of lights. Parking fills early on weekends, so arrive well before sunset.

spots.name: Hollywood Boulevard at the TCL Chinese Theatre
spots.tip: Work the stretch between the TCL Chinese Theatre and Highland Avenue handheld, framing marquees, neon and the Walk of Fame stars. The sidewalks are too crowded for a tripod.

spots.name: Bradbury Building
spots.tip: From the ground-floor lobby, point the 14-24 up at the iron staircases and the glass roof. Visitors stay on the ground floor and first landing.

spots.name: Walt Disney Concert Hall
spots.when: Late afternoon, low sun on the steel
spots.tip: Walk the stairs from Grand Avenue up to the rooftop garden and frame the curved steel panels catching the low sun. Look for reflections of neighbouring towers in the panels.

spots.name: Sixth Street Viaduct
spots.tip: Walk the bridge's pedestrian path and frame the lit arches leading west to the downtown skyline. Exposures of 10 to 20 seconds turn traffic into light trails.

days.title: Arrival, Painted Ladies and Twin Peaks

travel.label: Flight to San Francisco (SFO), then pick up the car

slots.label: Late afternoon
slots.why: The classic row of houses takes the late sun on its facades, an easy first stop after landing.

slots.label: Night
slots.why: The highest viewpoint in the city shows the whole lit grid on the first night.
slots.note: Drive up; the summit road is a short loop from the parking lot.

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: Your must-see Golden Gate Bridge at dawn, with fog rolling under the deck from the Marin side.
slots.note: Leave the city by 06:15; the Conzelman Road pullouts fill even at dawn on weekends.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.why: The bridge arch from below makes a strong daylight long exposure with the ND10.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: Sunset and blue hour on the bridge with rocks and surf in the foreground.

days.title: Chinatown, cable cars and the Bay Bridge

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: Sunday morning on Grant Avenue is busy with shoppers and deliveries, good street material.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.why: Cable cars cresting Russian Hill with Alcatraz behind is San Francisco street life in one frame.

slots.label: Night
slots.why: A calm pier and the lit Bay Bridge for a clean night long exposure.

days.title: Russian Hill dawn, Sutro Baths and the skyline

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: Sunrise behind the Bay Bridge from a quiet terrace on Russian Hill.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: Ruins and Pacific surf at sunset for long exposures on the western edge of the city.

slots.label: Night
slots.why: The full skyline across the bay at night, the widest city view of the trip.
slots.note: Treasure Island is reached from the Bay Bridge; take the Treasure Island exit in the middle of the bridge.

travel.label: Highway 1 via Half Moon Bay and Santa Cruz

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: A still lagoon and the rotunda at dawn before the drive south.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.why: The tall lighthouse on the San Mateo coast breaks up the drive south.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: Sunset over Carmel Bay, a short walk from the base.

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: Coves, cypress and surge channels in clear morning light from the reserve's opening.

slots.label: Late afternoon
slots.why: A quieter headland with side light on the rocks before the sunset stop.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: The arch and the coast at sunset is the defining Big Sur frame.
slots.note: About 30 minutes south of Carmel; turnouts on both sides are small.

days.title: Deep Big Sur and McWay Falls

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: The lighthouse on its rock is strongest in morning fog, shot long from the road.

slots.label: Late afternoon
slots.why: Keyhole Arch and backlit surf in low sun for long exposures.
slots.note: Sycamore Canyon Road is narrow and unsigned at the highway; there is a day-use fee at the gate.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: Your must-see McWay Falls in the last light, about 30 minutes south of Pfeiffer Beach.
slots.note: Allow 75 minutes for the drive back to Carmel in the dark.

travel.label: US-101 via Santa Barbara, then Highway 1 through Malibu

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: The Lone Cypress in soft morning light before the long drive south.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: Sea stacks and an arch at sunset where the drive rejoins the coast.

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: Reflections and footbridges on still canals before the neighbourhood wakes.

slots.label: Afternoon
slots.why: Saturday afternoon brings the most skaters and the best action.

slots.label: Blue hour
slots.why: The lit Ferris wheel and pier at blue hour for long exposures from the sand.

days.title: Hollywood from the hills to the boulevard

slots.label: Morning
slots.why: The Hollywood Sign is front-lit in the morning from this lawn.

slots.label: Sunset
slots.why: Sunset and the city lights coming on from the best viewpoint in Los Angeles.

slots.label: Night
slots.why: Neon, marquees and crowds for street photography after dark.

days.title: Downtown architecture and the Sixth Street Viaduct

slots.label: Midday
slots.why: Overhead light through the skylight fills the iron atrium at midday.

slots.label: Late afternoon
slots.why: Low sun turns the steel curves gold.

slots.label: Night
slots.why: Lit arches and traffic trails with the skyline behind close the trip.

skipped.name: Alcatraz Island
skipped.reason: Day tours sell out weeks ahead, and the island frames better from Hyde Street with the 100-400.

skipped.name: Muir Woods
skipped.reason: Needs a parking or shuttle reservation and half a day, which the Golden Gate and city plan uses better.

skipped.name: Point Bonita Lighthouse
skipped.reason: Opening hours are short and change often; Battery Spencer covers the Marin Headlands.

skipped.name: Elephant Seal Vista, Piedras Blancas
skipped.reason: South of the Big Sur stretch reachable from Carmel, and the drive to Los Angeles takes US-101.
